name: MonarchAiSafetyNotice
title: AiSafetyNotice
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column on the MonarchBanner surface, with MonarchButton and MonarchLink actions in a FlowRow; androidx.compose.ui.platform.LocalUriHandler opens the link
summary: Says, calmly and specifically, that a safety system blocked a request, changed an answer or removed parts of it, with an optional reason, next steps, an Edit prompt button and a link to the content guidelines.
whenToUse: In an AI conversation, where the answer would have been, when a safety or moderation system blocked the request or changed or shortened the answer.
whenNotToUse: For a failed turn (rate limit, lost connection, a safety block reported as an error code) use MonarchAiErrorMessage. For a general warning outside a conversation use MonarchBanner. For the standing "AI can make mistakes" note use MonarchAiDisclaimer.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiSafetyNotice(kind: MonarchAiSafetyNoticeKind, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, title: String? = null, message: String? = null, reason: String? = null, nextSteps: String? = null, learnMoreUrl: String? = null, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiSafetyNoticeLabels = MonarchAiSafetyNoticeLabels(), onEditPrompt: (() -> Unit)? = null, onOpenLearnMore: ((String) -> Unit)? = null)
enum class MonarchAiSafetyNoticeKind { Blocked, Modified, Filtered }

class MonarchAiSafetyNoticeLabels(title: ((kind: MonarchAiSafetyNoticeKind) -> String)? = null, message: ((kind: MonarchAiSafetyNoticeKind) -> String)? = null, reason: String? = null, editPrompt: String? = null, learnMore: String? = null)

options.name: kind
options.description: What the safety system did. Sets the tone and the built-in title and explanation.

options.name: title
options.description: Replaces the title of the kind for this notice.

options.name: message
options.description: Replaces the explanation of the kind for this notice.

options.name: reason
options.description: Why, in plain words, shown after a bold "Reason:" label. Blank text is not shown.

options.name: nextSteps
options.description: What the person can do next, as a sentence. Blank text is not shown.

options.name: learnMoreUrl
options.description: Adds a "Content guidelines" link. Only http, https and mailto links are shown.

options.name: icon
options.description: An icon at the start in the tone color, for example a lock. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replaces the built-in titles, explanations, "Reason:", "Edit prompt" and "Content guidelines".

options.name: onEditPrompt
options.description: Adds an "Edit prompt" button, usually to put the prompt back in the composer.

options.name: onOpenLearnMore
options.description: Called with the link instead of opening it with LocalUriHandler, for example to open a Custom Tab.

states.name: static
states.description: Without onEditPrompt and a safe learnMoreUrl the notice has no action row.

appearance: The surface of MonarchBanner: the subtle fill and the border of the warning tone for a blocked request and of the info tone otherwise, the strong role of the tone for the icon, default text for the title and the bold "Reason:" label, muted text for the explanation, reason and next steps. Edit prompt is a small secondary button and the guidelines a standalone link.
platformNotes: The parity map names MonarchBanner, but the banner takes one string and one action, so the notice draws the same surface and tone palette and adds its own text and actions, as MonarchAiErrorMessage does. The web takes rich content for the reason and next steps; Android takes plain strings, as iOS does. The web's children replace the explanation; here that is message. learnMoreUrl is a String (iOS takes a URL) and opens through LocalUriHandler or onOpenLearnMore instead of a new tab. The web and iOS draw a glyph per kind; Monarch for Android bundles no icons, so the icon is a slot and each kind is told by its title. Same names as iOS.
accessibility: The title, the explanation, the reason with its "Reason:" label and the next steps are one TalkBack element, read in that order.
Edit prompt is a separate button and the guidelines link a separate link read with "opens in the browser"; both have 48dp touch targets.
Each kind has its own title, so the kind does not depend on color or on the icon; the icon slot is decoration.
The notice does not announce itself; place it where the answer would have been.
edgeCases: A reason or next steps that are empty or only white space are not shown.
A javascript:, file: or custom-scheme link is dropped and no link is shown; spaces around a link are trimmed.
The actions sit on one line when they fit and wrap when they do not, at large text sizes.
title and message given to the notice win over the labels.

examples.title: Blocked request with next steps
examples.template:
MonarchAiSafetyNotice(
    kind = MonarchAiSafetyNoticeKind.{{kind|pascal}},
    reason = {{reason}},
    nextSteps = {{nextSteps}},
    learnMoreUrl = {{learnMoreHref}},
    icon = { MonarchIcon(SampleIcons.Lock, contentDescription = null) },
    onEditPrompt = {},
)
examples.code:
MonarchAiSafetyNotice(
    kind = MonarchAiSafetyNoticeKind.Blocked,
    reason = "The request asked for someone’s home address.",
    nextSteps = "Ask about public information instead, such as a company’s office location.",
    learnMoreUrl = "https://example.com/guidelines",
    icon = { MonarchIcon(SampleIcons.Lock, contentDescription = null) },
    onEditPrompt = {},
)

examples.title: Hidden content with a custom explanation
examples.code:
MonarchAiSafetyNotice(
    kind = MonarchAiSafetyNoticeKind.Filtered,
    message = "Two links were removed from this answer.",
)
